issues.failure_explanation: With Phi=(1/2pi)ln|x-y| and outward n_y, the paper itself uses int_{dOmega} dPhi/dn_y = 1 (interior) and 1/2 (boundary). Then the interior limit of the double layer W(x)=int beta dPhi/dn_y is W(x*) + beta(x*)/2, not u(x*) - beta(x*)/2 as displayed. Taking (BIE-limit) literally and letting u(x)->f(x*) yields beta = 2*int Phi psi (no f), contradicting the BIE stated immediately after with 'Hence'. The inference from the displayed limit to (BIE) is therefore invalid as written; the BIE itself is correct under the correct jump relation.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side of (BIE-limit) by int_{dOmega} beta(y) dPhi/dn_y(x*,y) dsigma_y + beta(x*)/2 (or equivalently state f(x*) = W(x*) + beta(x*)/2 + volume term), consistent with the sign convention used in the proofs.
issues.overall_effect: Only the stated jump relation in Theorem BIM and its 'Hence' inference are wrong; the BIE and all later constructions use the correct relation, so no downstream result fails.
issues.title: Stated jump relation (BIE-limit) is inconsistent with the paper's sign convention and with the BIE derived from it
issues.why_classification: A local restatement of a recalled classical formula fixes the inconsistency; no result or guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: For the Poisson BIE on the unit disc the kernel is the constant 2*(1/4pi)=1/(2pi), so T beta = g - (1/2pi) int_{dOmega} beta dsigma and sup|T b1 - T b2| = |mean(b1-b2)| attains ||b1-b2|| for constants: q = 1 exactly (this holds for any convex domain since the double-layer kernel is nonnegative with integral 1/2). The Fredholm NN error bound (fnn-error), which the paper uses to quantify ||beta-beta_M|| and to 'explain' the Poisson error decay, contains 1/(1-q) and e^{-(1-q)v_M} and is vacuous/undefined at q=1; the proposition's claim that the kernel satisfies what the FNN framework requires therefore does not deliver convergence or a rate for the Poisson case.

failure_location.quote: It can easily be shown that the kernel is non-expansive (see detailed calculations in section \ref{numerics-section}), as required under the Fredholm NN framework.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a separate convergence/error argument for the q=1 Poisson operator, e.g. exploiting that on the disc T is affine with a rank-one integral part so the Krasnoselskii–Mann iterate converges geometrically with rate max(|1-2kappa|,1-kappa), and use this in place of (fnn-error) for the Poisson bound.
issues.overall_effect: For the Poisson PDE (the paper's first example and its explainability discussion), the source provides no valid bound on ||beta-beta_M|| and hence no explicit error bound for the PFNN; the Helmholtz case (where q<1 because Phi<0) is unaffected.
issues.title: Poisson BIE operator has Lipschitz constant exactly 1, so the cited Fredholm NN convergence/error bound (fnn-error) is undefined for the Poisson case
issues.why_classification: A contained new lemma (convergence of the FNN iteration at q=1) is needed; without it the explicit Poisson error bound and its explainability claim are unsupported, but the construction and Helmholtz results survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: 0 = \int_{\partial \Omega} \mathcal{L}\Phi(x,y) d\sigma_y = \int_{\Omega - B(x,\epsilon)} \Delta_y \Phi(x, y) dy - \lambda \int_{\partial B(x,\epsilon)} \frac{\partial \Phi(x,y)}{\partial n_y} d\sigma_y.

issues.failure_explanation: Step 2 computes 0 = int_{dOmega} dPhi/dn + int_{Xi} dPhi/dn - int Phi with int_{Xi} ≈ -1/2, which gives int_{dOmega} dPhi/dn(x*,y) = +1/2 + lambda int Phi, yet the conclusion is written with -1/2. The final representation (potential-limit-expression) uses C_1(x)-C_2(x*) = 1/2 + lambda int deltaPhi, which requires +1/2; with the stated -1/2 the coefficient would be 3/2 + lambda int deltaPhi. In Step 1 the identity 0=int_{dOmega} L Phi dsigma is meaningless (should be the volume integral over Omega\B) and the lambda factor is dropped in the volume term, and the fundamental solution is given with argument lambda|x-y| in one place and sqrt(lambda)|x-y| in another. The final formula is correct, but the written derivation does not validly establish it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Rewrite Steps 1–2: apply the divergence theorem to int_{Omega\B} L Phi dy = 0, keep the factor lambda on the volume term, take epsilon->0, and state int_{dOmega} dPhi/dn(x*,y) = +1/2 + lambda int_Omega Phi(x*,y) dy; use sqrt(lambda) consistently.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Proposition semi-linear-pot as written does not support its conclusion; the conclusion itself (and Theorem error-bounds-thrm which builds on it) is correct once the identities are fixed.
issues.title: Derivation of the Helmholtz boundary integral identities is internally inconsistent (wrong sign of 1/2, missing lambda, wrong integration domains, lambda vs sqrt(lambda))
issues.why_classification: Routine local corrections to a derivation whose end result is correct; no claim is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The step int |(beta-beta_M)(y) - (beta-beta_M)(x*)| D Phi dsigma <= 2||beta-beta_M|| ||int D Phi dsigma|| requires D Phi >= 0. Nonnegativity of each normal derivative dPhi/dn_y(x,y) and dPhi/dn_y(x*,y) does not imply nonnegativity of their difference D Phi, so the stated justification is invalid. For non-convex domains even dPhi/dn_y changes sign, although the paper claims applicability to arbitrary geometries. The correct general bound needs ||int |D Phi| dsigma||_Omega (and ||int |dPhi/dn_y| dsigma|| in the 4th term).

failure_location.quote: where for the last steps we recall that the normal derivative of the fundamental solution is non-negative (see calculations for the potential above).

issues.overall_effect: The constants in (error-domain) are justified only when D Phi >= 0 (true for the Poisson disc where D Phi is half the Poisson kernel); in general the bound must use absolute values.
issues.title: Bound on the first error term drops absolute values using nonnegativity of dPhi/dn, but D Phi is a difference of normal derivatives
issues.why_classification: Inserting absolute values is a one-line fix preserving the form and content of the error bound.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Step 1. Construct the PDE (\ref{iteration}) with source term $\psi_n(x) := -\lambda u_n(x) + F(x,u_n(x))$.

issues.failure_explanation: In Algorithm alg:nl-algo the source at step n is built from the computed approximation tilde u_{n-1}, not from the exact iterate u_{n-1}. Hence ||tilde u_n - u_n|| is not a single PFNN error epsilon: tilde u_n = PFNN(T applied to tilde u_{n-1}), so ||tilde u_n - u_n|| <= epsilon_n + q||tilde u_{n-1} - u_{n-1}||, giving an accumulated error sum_{k} q^{n-k} epsilon_k <= sup_k epsilon_k/(1-q). The proof's decomposition treats ||tilde u_n - u_n|| as bounded by (error-domain) directly, which is unjustified; moreover epsilon^{RPFNN} depends on n (through psi_n, beta_M and the D_i), so a uniform-in-n bound is required but not established.

failure_location.quote: Substituting the error bound (\ref{error-domain}) and using the known error bound for the fixed point iterations results in (\ref{error-recurrent}).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove by induction ||tilde u_n - u_n|| <= sum_{k=1}^n q^{n-k} epsilon_k <= (sup_k epsilon_k)/(1-q), with epsilon_k the PFNN error of iteration k, establish a uniform bound on epsilon_k (uniform bounds on beta_M and D_i over the iterates), and restate (error-recurrent) accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated RPFNN interior error bound (error-recurrent) is not proved; the true bound carries an extra factor 1/(1-q) and a supremum over iterations. The boundary bound is essentially unaffected since each PFNN output satisfies (error-boundary) for whatever source is used.
issues.title: RPFNN error bound ignores propagation of the per-iteration PFNN error through the recurrent fixed-point iteration
issues.why_classification: A contained but nontrivial additional argument (error accumulation with uniform per-iteration bounds) is needed and the constant worsens by 1/(1-q); the result remains recognizably comparable.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Here, we select a straightforward quadrature rule, across the points at which $u_n(x)$ has been calculated in order to avoid any interpolation-like approximations.
Step 4. Solve the PDE using the PFNN to estimate $u_n(r_i, \theta_j)$ for $i \in \{1, \ldots M_r\}$, $j \in \{1, \ldots M_{\theta} \}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The quadrature nodes (r,theta) in R x Theta are the same grid points at which u is evaluated (Step 4), so for each target x=(r_i,theta_j) the sum contains the term with y = x, where Phi(x,x) = -(1/2pi)K_0(0) = +infinity (or ln 0 for Poisson). The Riemann sum as written is therefore undefined; the algorithm does not specify how the singular node is excluded or treated, unlike the linear examples where adaptive quadrature is described. Index bookkeeping in the loop (Step 4 computes u_n rather than u_{n+1}, and the loop over n<=N' returns u_{N'}) is also inconsistent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify the treatment of the y=x cell (e.g. omit it or replace it by the analytic integral of Phi over the cell, which is O(h^2 log h)), and fix the iteration indices in the pseudocode.
issues.overall_effect: Step 2 of Algorithm alg:nl-algo is not well defined at the target node; the reported RPFNN results depend on an unstated treatment of the singular term.
issues.title: Volume quadrature in the Recurrent PFNN evaluates the singular fundamental solution at the target node itself
issues.why_classification: A standard local quadrature fix restores well-definedness without affecting any stated guarantee.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \frac{\partial \Phi(x,y)}{\partial n_y} = -\frac{\sqrt{\lambda} K_0' \left( \sqrt{\lambda} |x - y| \right)}{2\pi |x - y|} \big( y_1 (y_1 - x_1) + y_2 (y_2 - x_2) \big).
we therefore have a weakly singular kernel in the integral operator for the BIE (in contrast to the Poisson PDE, as seen above)

issues.failure_explanation: From the paper's own correct first display, dPhi/dn_y = sqrt(lambda) K_1(sqrt(lambda)|x-y|) (y·(y-x))/(2pi|x-y|); with |x|=|y|=1, y·(y-x) = |x-y|^2/2, giving dPhi/dn_y = sqrt(lambda) K_1(sqrt(lambda)|x-y|)|x-y|/(4pi), a bounded kernel tending to 1/(4pi) as x->y (consistent with the paper's own limit). The displayed formula instead has |x-y|^2 in the denominator of the first factor and yields sqrt(lambda)K_1/(4pi|x-y|) ~ 1/(4pi|x-y|^2), which is non-integrable on the boundary, contradicting the stated finite limit 1/(4pi), the 'weakly singular' description, and the asserted non-expansiveness of the BIE operator. The kernel used to construct the FNN weights is therefore misstated.

failure_location.quote: \frac{\partial \Phi(x,y)}{\partial n_y} = \frac{\sqrt{\lambda} K_1 \left( \sqrt{\lambda} |x - y| \right)}{2\pi |x - y|^2} \left( y_1 (y_1 - x_1) + y_2 (y_2 - x_2) \right) = \frac{\sqrt{\lambda} K_1 \left( \sqrt{\lambda} |x - y| \right)}{4\pi |x - y|}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the boundary kernel to sqrt(lambda) K_1(sqrt(lambda)|x-y|)|x-y|/(4pi) (value 1/(4pi) at x=y) and remove the claim that the BIE kernel is weakly singular.
issues.overall_effect: The numerical construction of the Helmholtz BIE kernel as written is incorrect and the described singularity handling is unnecessary/misdirected; the reported results can only correspond to the corrected bounded kernel.
issues.title: Helmholtz boundary kernel formula is wrong by a factor |x-y|^2 and the 'weakly singular kernel' claim is false
issues.why_classification: A local algebraic correction restores a bounded, correct kernel and all stated guarantees survive.
